quotes.citation: ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་ཉི་ཤུ་ལྔ་པ། (Kangyur, NYI KHRI vol. KA) — the close of the five-eyes passage
quotes.why: The sūtra sentence the paragraph quotes, in the Kangyur Pañcaviṃśati itself: note བརྩོན་པར་བྱའོ 'should strive' where the yig cha has བསླབ་པར་བྱའོ, and ཐོབ་པར without རབ་ཏུ. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་ཉི་ཤུ་ལྔ་པ། (Kangyur, NYI KHRI vol. KA) — the lines immediately following
quotes.why: The sūtra's own reason for the causal claim: the perfection of wisdom generates the other perfections and the five eyes — and the next sentence is the one Tsongkhapa and Gyaltsab turn into the 'purpose' of p414. Found by direct search.

Chökyi Gyaltsen's own presentation of the sūtra, a few pages earlier, where the same sentence is placed as the summary (དོན་བསྡུས) of the whole five-eyes passage — with the same བསླབ་པར and རབ་ཏུ readings as p413.
The outline that fixes what p413's བཞི་པ་ནི is fourth of: definition, divisions, boundaries, cause, and the purpose of arising from the cause. Found by reading the pack's tier-1 lead in context.
The yig cha opening this whole excursus on the root-text words སྤྱན་ལྔ་དང་ནི, and framing the five eyes as the cause of not depending on others in practice.
The Ornament's verse on the ten instructions; the five eyes are the seventh, and the root text says nothing about their causes.
Haribhadra's whole gloss on the five eyes gives their objects and nothing on their causes; the one causal word in it, རྣམ་པར་སྨིན་པ, attaches to the divine eye.

Tsongkhapa's statement of the cause of the five eyes, which p413 reproduces almost word for word — except that Chökyi Gyaltsen drops ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་མེད་པ and the attribution of the legs of miraculous power to the Great Commentary.

The Great Commentary gloss Tsongkhapa is pointing to: the flesh eye as the ripened eye produced by the power of cultivating the legs of miraculous power. Found by direct search; its Indian source was not located in this archive.

Gyaltsab Je goes straight from the boundaries (quoted in p412) to the purpose (quoted in p414): he states no cause at all, which is why p413, alone of its neighbours, is not built on the རྣམ་བཤད. Found by direct search.
An Indian commentary on the Śatasāhasrikā (attributed to Daṃṣṭrasena) reading the same sūtra line causally — the five eyes are attained by practising the six perfections.

quotes.citation: འཕགས་པ་གྲོལ་སྡེ། ཉི་ཁྲི་སྣང་བ། (Tengyur, SHES PHYIN vol. KA) — the flesh eye under the instruction on the five eyes
quotes.why: Ārya Vimuktisena explaining the flesh eye's fixed range as born of karmic ripening or as a dominant-condition effect — the Indian root of the later question how a ripened organ can be the fruit of path practice.
Jamyang Shepa's consequence against anyone who takes the flesh eye to be simply a ripened effect: it would then be ethically neutral, yet it is a path and so virtuous.
Jamyang Shepa rejecting the view that the flesh eye is the physical organ ripened from cultivating the legs of miraculous power — the reading one could draw from Tsongkhapa's Great Commentary gloss.

Jamyang Shepa's own solution: the six perfections and the Mahāyāna legs of miraculous power ripen into a special eye-organ, and the flesh eye is the awareness that organ serves as dominant condition for.

Chökyi Gyaltsen's own definition of the flesh eye as an awareness relying on a flesh eye-organ as its uncommon dominant condition — which already separates the organ from the eye-awareness that p413 gives a cause for.
Chökyi Gyaltsen's Mahāyāna placement: the legs of miraculous power, third of the 37 factors' groups, are principally cultivated on the great accumulation path. Found by direct search.
Chökyi Gyaltsen's Abhidharma placement of the same factors, where the legs of miraculous power begin only at the peak stage of the preparation path.
